instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until you serve.

Cut the eggplants into 1 inch pieces. Pat the tofu dry with paper towels and cut it into 1/2 inch cubes. Finely chop the onion, mince the 3 garlic cloves, and slice the scallions, keeping the whites and greens apart.
In a small bowl, stir the 1 1/2 tbsp potato starch into 3 tbsp cold water.

Heat 3 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the eggplant and the 1/2 tsp salt and cook, stirring often, until the pieces are golden and tender but still a little firm, about 8 minutes. Transfer them to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the same skillet. Add the onion and the scallion whites and cook for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, 2 tsp of the doubanjiang, the 1 tbsp sake, 2 tsp sugar and 3 tbsp soy sauce. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells rich and fragrant.
Pour in the 2 1/4 cups broth. Add the eggplant and tofu and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 6 minutes.
Stir the starch mixture again and pour it in slowly, stirring, until the sauce is glossy and thick, about 30 seconds.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the 1 tsp rice vinegar and the 1/2 tsp sesame oil.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the eggplant and tofu over the rice and sprinkle with the scallion greens. Stir the last 1 tsp doubanjiang into your own bowl if you want it hotter.
method_notes: Pickled Plum is the lead: eggplant is browned first and set aside, a doubanjiang and garlic base is cooked in the same pan, then everything simmers in stock and is thickened with starch and finished with rice vinegar and sesame oil. Its rating is only 5 from 2 reviews, so this counts as a fallback, and none of the other versions had 20 ratings. The tofu comes from Ellie Likes Cooking's Japanese style vegan version, in place of the lead's textured vegetable protein. Oyster sauce is dropped (an extra tablespoon of soy sauce replaces it), vegetable broth replaces chicken stock, and the bamboo shoots are left out. Check the doubanjiang label if the dish has to be strictly vegan.
